title: A 94.8nW Battery-Free Intelligent Silicon Platform Enabling Distributed, Adaptive, and Event-Driven Multimodal Sensing at the Edge
problem: Ultra-low-power (ULP) edge sensors with ML must operate from 100nW harvested energy while supporting distributed, multimodal sensing and model adaptation. Current systems suffer from isolated monomodal operation, limited task complexity, and high power overhead of NN accelerators that prevent network expansion.
motivation: Distributed edge ML requires efficient fusion of multimodal sensor data across networks with adaptive models for real-world data drift, yet existing ULP NN accelerators consume excessive power, limiting system scalability.
method: A 94.8nW battery-free platform integrates adaptive event-driven multimodal sensing with an ultra-low-power NN accelerator. The design enables model adaptation for handling data distribution shifts while supporting collaborative sensing across distributed sensor nodes through efficient power management.
key_novelty: Ultra-low-power distributed multimodal sensing platform with adaptive ML supporting energy-harvested edge operation and fused multi-sensor inference.
contributions: Battery-free 94.8nW operation on harvested energy down to 100nW ambient level
Adaptive NN models supporting data drift correction in real-world environments
Multimodal sensor fusion enabling complex task detection vs. isolated monomodal sensing
Distributed collaborative sensing across sensor networks with low power overhead
baselines: Prior ULP NN accelerators (high power consumption)
limitations: Not discussed; accuracy degradation on diverse workloads, model update latency, and network coordination overhead not characterized.
